unit.can_do_en: talk about tomorrow, next week and next year.

lines.speaker: Aino
lines.gloss_en: What are you doing at the weekend?

judge.reason: Only register differs (sä/sinä); same question about weekend plans.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.gloss_en: On Saturday I'm going to a flea market.

judge.reason: mä meen/minä menen and kirpparille/kirpputorille are register variants; same meaning (Saturday, flea market).

lines.speaker: Aino
lines.gloss_en: Nice! What are you looking for?

judge.reason: etit/etsit and sä/sinä are register variants; same question.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.text_puhe: Pöytää ja tuoleja. Mä tarviin niitä uuteen asuntoon.
lines.text_kirja: Pöytää ja tuoleja. Minä tarvitsen niitä uuteen asuntoon.
lines.gloss_en: A table and chairs. I need them for my new flat.

judge.reason: tarviin/tarvitsen is a register difference; same content: tables and chairs for the new apartment.

puhe.text: Pöytää ja tuoleja. Mä tarviin niitä uuteen asuntoon.

kirja.text: Pöytää ja tuoleja. Minä tarvitsen niitä uuteen asuntoon.

judge.reason: Only sä/sinä differs; same question about moving.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.gloss_en: Yes, next month. To a bigger flat.

judge.reason: Joo/kyllä and ens kuus/ensi kuussa are register variants; same time (next month) and bigger apartment.

lines.speaker: Aino
lines.gloss_en: Do you need help with the move?

judge.reason: Tarviik sä apuu muutos is colloquial for Tarvitsetko sinä apua muutossa; same question about needing help with the move.
Joo/kyllä and ois/olisi are register differences; same meaning.

forms.why_en: The partitive of mikä, what. Mitä saa olla? means What can I get you?
Speech shortens sinä to sä. Books write sinä.
Tehdä changes to tee- and takes -t for 'you': teet.
Viikonloppu with -na for 'at, on' a time: viikonloppuna.
Days take -na for 'on': lauantai becomes lauantaina.
Speech shortens minä to mä. Books write minä.
Mennä, to go, with -n for 'I': menen. Speech says meen.
Adds -lle for 'to': kirpputori becomes kirpputorille. Speech says kirppari, giving kirpparille.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Etsiä means to look for. -t goes with sinä. Speech drops the s: etit.
Looking for something takes -ä: pöytä becomes pöytää.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Plural 'some' takes -ja: tuoli becomes tuoleja, i turning into e.
Adds -n for 'I': tarvita becomes tarvitsen. Speech says tarviin.
The partitive plural of ne 'they': niitä, used after kokeilla 'to try'.
Adds -en to match asuntoon: uusi becomes uuteen.
Adds -on for 'into' or 'for': asunto becomes asuntoon.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Muuttaa means to move house. -t goes with sinä: muutat.
Joo is the everyday spoken yes. Books write kyllä.
Speech drops the final i: ensi becomes ens.
Adds -ssa for time: kuu becomes kuussa. Speech says ens kuus.
Iso means big. -mpa- makes 'bigger' and -an adds 'to': isompaan.

forms.form_name_en: present tense, 2nd person singular, with the question ending -ko/-kö
forms.why_en: Tarvita means to need. Books write tarvitsetko. Speech says tarviiksä.
After tarvita 'to need', the noun takes the partitive singular: apu becomes apua. Speech says apuu.
Adds -ssa for 'in' or 'with': muutto becomes muutossa, tt turning into t. Speech says muutos.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
The conditional adds -isi for 'would': olla becomes olisi. Speech shortens olisi to ois.
The partitive singular is used in exclamations: ihana becomes ihanaa!
